page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configuration built on the x86_64 architecture using Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at frequencies up to 4.2 GHz across 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The processor architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache, complemented by Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector acceleration. The system allocates 64 GB of RAM, resulting in a compact 2 GB per vCPU ratio. A key architectural component is the inclusion of 1,888 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage, while dedicated GPU accelerators are absent.

Benchmark results highlight strong computational and data handling metrics. Geekbench multi-core evaluation reached 17,402 points, supported by high-tier results in image processing and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 203.81 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput performed well within the upper quartile at 54.77 GB/sec, while large-block uncached memory read bandwidth achieved 211.12 GB/sec. Hardware-level matrix instructions yield strong small-model LLM inference generation speeds of 396.8 tokens per second. However, throughput scales down on large parameter models, where 70B text generation registers at 2.77 tokens per second.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio represents an engineering tradeoff designed for compute density rather than large in-memory structures. Delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs with high-speed local NVMe disk without the overhead of surplus RAM maximizes compute and I/O efficiency for specialized workloads. The platform is well matched for continuous integration build runners, batch data transformations, media encoding, static web delivery, and distributed compute worker nodes requiring high throughput scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is a compute-focused instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 64 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, alongside 1,888 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. It lacks dedicated hardware GPUs but includes advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks demonstrate strong performance in uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 211.12 GB/sec for reads, as well as competitive throughput in static web serving and multithreaded compression. Image processing scores rank within the top decile. The 2 GB per vCPU allocation represents a clear tradeoff, making this instance less appropriate for large in-memory databases, yet cost-efficient for CPU-intensive processing, batch compute, CI/CD compilation, and web serving pipelines that benefit from fast local temporary storage.
